world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

new_statements.quote: 2. TONALITE. Sur le plan tonal, le holoholo a conservé en général les tons du protobantou. On peut observer, dans les formes suivantes, que les tons structurels des radicaux verbaux du holoholo sont identiques à ceux attestés en protobantou, à cela près qu'ils se déplacent vers la droite d'une syllabe : [...] Le holoholo atteste en effet un déplacement tonal généralisé des tons vers la droite d'une ou de deux syllabes.
new_statements.translation: 2. TONALITY. On the tonal level, Holoholo has in general preserved the tones of Proto-Bantu. One can observe in the following forms that the structural tones of Holoholo verb radicals are identical to those attested in Proto-Bantu, except that they shift one syllable to the right: [...] Holoholo indeed shows a generalized shift of tones to the right by one or two syllables.
new_statements.citation: Kamba Muzenga, Jean-Georges. 1987. Phonologie historique du holoholo. Annales Aequatoria 8: 317-348.
new_statements.locator: §2 'Tonalité', p. 324 (PDF p. 8 of the extracted article; p. 320 of the volume PDF)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Holoholo is described as a two-tone (H/L, plus a rising tone from H-shift) language in which Proto-Bantu tones are retained but realised one or two syllables to the right of their etymological position (e.g. *HB > BH, *HH > BH, *BH > BA/BB in noun stems; ku-twal-a > kutwalá). No stress or accent is mentioned anywhere in the article; nothing places a word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Tonal only: stems with only low tones (*B, *BB) keep Proto-Bantu tones unchanged (p. 326); the author flags the apparent 'inversion tonale' as needing further study.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (noun and verb stems, cited in isolation and in short verb forms); the data are Coupez 1955's, the author had no informants; the article is a historical phonology, not a synchronic description of prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: All data trace to Coupez 1955, i.e. West Holoholo of the Kalemie region, DR Congo (Guthrie D28a; Kamba Muzenga 1987 p. 317: 'parlée dans la région de Kalemie au Shaba'). East Holoholo/Guha (D28b, Tanzania) has only 19th-century wordlists (Stanley, Johnston, Jones). Glottolog's country codes BW/ZW and the alt-names Kalanga/Kikalanga reflect confusion with Kalanga S16 (kala1405, kck) of Botswana/Zimbabwe: the Botswana refs Hasselbring 2000 and Batibo & Mosaka 2000 do not concern this language. Omasombo 2014 (p. 119) also separates DRC 'kalanga (D28)' of Nyunzu from holoholo, citing Coupez 1955 and Kamba Muzenga 1987.

sources.citation: Kamba Muzenga, Jean-Georges. 1987. Phonologie historique du holoholo. Annales Aequatoria 8: 317-348.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (the words 'accent', 'intensité', 'pénultième' do not occur). Section 2 'Tonalité' (pp. 324-326) treats Holoholo as a H/L tone language that keeps Proto-Bantu tones but shifts them one or two syllables to the right; data are taken entirely from Coupez 1955 (author states he had no Holoholo informants).

sources.note: Held part contains only the Maho classification list (D28a West Holoholo, Guha, Kalanga; D28b East Holoholo, Tanzania) and the Coupez 1955 bibliography entry; pp. 64 and 190 (tone chapter) are not in the held file.

sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Holoholo' (hol), all datapoints sourced to Coupez 1955 (local CLDF).
sources.note: Holoholo is coded only for word-order/morphology features (81A-90C, 112A, 143A-144K) from Coupez 1955 pp. 67, 120-137; no values for 13A tone or 14A-16A stress, i.e. Goedemans & van der Hulst did not code it.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A comparative study of the Bantu and semi-Bantu languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. Language 40 'Guha' (vocabulary, prefixes p. 196; bibliography p. 792).
sources.note: No Guha-specific statement; only his general transcription convention in the introduction that the Bantu 'accent or pitch of the voice... is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when an exception... transfers the voice-pitch to the first, last, or other syllable' — generic, not a Holoholo description.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 CLDF references (sources.bib), 38 entries tagged holo1240/Holoholo.
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Descriptive items: Coupez 1955 (grammar), Kamba Muzenga 1987 (comparative), Schmitz 1912 (ethnographic), Delhaise 1908 (ethnographic), Meeussen 1953 Kongo-Overzee 19 (overview, minimal), Jones 1889 unpublished Guha vocabulary, Johnston 1897/1919 wordlists; the Botswana items (Hasselbring 2000, Batibo & Mosaka 2000) are misassigned via the alt-name Kalanga.
